patients.summary: Construction supervisor and heavy daily drinker who joined in 2022 with hypertension and asthma, was found to have acromegaly from a pituitary macroadenoma, then an ANCA vasculitis with kidney involvement. After his last practice visit in June 2024 the practice only receives records: alcohol pancreatitis, pituitary apoplexy with adrenal crisis, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with tumor lysis, and a shoulder dislocation with a cuff tear.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
50 y/o M here to establish. Construction supervisor, married.

He came in mostly because his hands and knees ache, worst first thing in the morning, going on about four months. Has had to take his wedding band off because it no longer goes past the knuckle, and he went up a size and a half in work boots this spring. Says his brother looked like this before he was diagnosed with acromegaly in his mid-forties, and his wife made him promise to mention it. No headaches or vision change he has noticed. Snores, unchanged.

PMH: hypertension for years on lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25, home readings 'fine.' Asthma since he was a teenager, albuterol a few times a month, more with dust on site. No hospitalizations, no surgeries.
Alcohol: drinks every day, by his count 6 beers on a light night and closer to 12 on weekends, with some heavier stretches recently. Has never tried to quit, no withdrawal he recognizes, no DUIs. AUDIT-C 11. Never smoked. No drugs.
FHx: father HTN, stroke at 68. Mother autoimmune thyroid disease. Brother acromegaly, dx at 45.
NKDA.

Exam: big-framed man, coarse facial features with a prominent jaw. Teeth spaced. Hands broad and fleshy. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. Knees bulky without effusion, full ROM. No edema. PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. Acral enlargement, arthralgia, with a first-degree relative with acromegaly. This needs a proper look. Referred to endocrinology, asked them to see him soon.
2. HTN: near goal. Continue current meds. CMP today.
3. Alcohol use disorder, severe by history. We talked about what the beer is doing to his pressure and his liver and that cutting down is worth it on its own. Offered naltrexone 50 mg daily; he would rather try on his own first. Door left open.
4. Asthma, intermittent: albuterol only, fine.
5. Health maintenance: CBC, lipids, A1c, one-time HCV and HIV screens. FIT kit given. Records requested from prior office. Flu and COVID in the fall.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Keith, your labs from Tuesday look good: kidney function normal (creatinine 1.0), blood counts normal, liver tests and sugar in range, cholesterol acceptable. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. Endocrinology should be calling you to schedule. Let me know if you haven't heard by the end of the month.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: FIT negative. Letter mailed to patient. Repeat in one year per PCP.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records from prior primary care office, 2015 to 2021, 41 pages, scanned.
Summary for chart: hypertension on lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, stable doses for several years. Asthma, albuterol as needed. Alcohol use noted at several visits with advice to cut back. Tdap 4/2018. No colon screening on file. Most recent BMP 2021 unremarkable. No allergies listed.
Reviewed and filed. - PCP

reports.text: Bilateral hands, 3 views each. Joint spaces of the hands are widened. No significant osteophyte formation. No erosions. Soft tissues prominent. Bone mineralization normal.
reports.conclusion: Widened joint spaces without significant osteophytes.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Date of visit: 9/5/2022
Reason for referral: possible acromegaly

Thank you for sending Mr. Bianchi, 50. He describes half a year of steadily worsening stiffness and pain in both knees and both hands, most noticeable on waking. His ring will no longer go on and his shoe size has gone up. His brother carries a diagnosis of acromegaly.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, albuterol inhaler as needed. NKDA. Never smoker; drinks heavily on a daily basis. Construction supervisor.

BP 140/85, HR 78.
Exam: prognathic jaw and macroglossia. Soft-tissue thickening of both hands. Knees with bony enlargement, range of motion preserved.

Results: IGF-1 elevated for age. Random GH elevated. On a 75 g oral glucose load GH failed to suppress.
Hand and knee radiographs: widened joint spaces, no significant osteophytes.

Impression: acromegaly, biochemically confirmed.
Plan: dedicated pituitary MRI. Visual fields if the adenoma approaches the chiasm. Will see him back with imaging to discuss treatment.

Allergies: NKDA

reports.study: MRI pituitary with and without contrast
reports.text:
Indication: acromegaly.
Technique: thin-section sagittal and coronal T1 and T2 imaging through the sella before and after gadolinium, dynamic coronal post-contrast series.
Findings: 1.8 cm sellar mass enhancing less than the normal gland, with mild suprasellar extension. The optic chiasm sits above the mass without compression. Cavernous sinuses unremarkable. No hemorrhage. Brain parenchyma otherwise unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 1.8 cm sellar mass with mild suprasellar extension, chiasm not compressed, consistent with pituitary macroadenoma.

documents.title: MRI reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pituitary MRI reviewed: 1.8 cm macroadenoma, chiasm clear. Fits the endocrine picture. Endocrinology letter arrived today too. They will go over treatment with him. Portal note sent to pt.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Date of visit: 11/8/2022

Follow-up for acromegaly. MRI 9/16 showed a 1.8 cm macroadenoma with mild suprasellar extension, chiasm clear. He saw neurosurgery on 10/20, who recommended transsphenoidal resection. He has declined surgery for now; he does not want time off work and is uneasy about an operation. We discussed that surgery offers the best chance of cure, and that medical therapy controls GH in many patients but rarely shrinks the tumor away.

Plan: octreotide LAR 20 mg IM every 4 weeks starting today, first dose given in clinic. Gallbladder symptoms reviewed. IGF-1 in 3 months to titrate. Revisit surgery at each visit.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, albuterol as needed, octreotide LAR as above. NKDA.

Faxed at the request of the primary care office.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 10 days of stuffy nose, thick discharge, pressure over the cheeks and forehead, worse bending over. Thought it was a cold, not getting better. No fever. Mild cough. Using albuterol a little more.
Also tells me he has been getting a monthly shot at endocrinology since November for the pituitary tumor. We had not received a note about that; added octreotide LAR to his list and asked the front desk to request the visit note. He saw neurosurgery and doesn't want surgery right now.

O: Afebrile. Maxillary and frontal tenderness. Turbinates swollen, purulent drainage. TMs clear. Lungs with no wheeze today. 

A/P: Sinusitis, past the window where it usually clears on its own. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 twice a day x 10 days, saline rinses. Call if not improving. BP 140s, recheck at next visit.
Octreotide noted, endocrine to manage.

documents.title: Still congested
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the antibiotic last week, still plugged up and the stuff coming out is the same. Coughing more too. Can I get something else? I can't really get off the site this week.

documents.title: RE: Still congested
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry it hasn't cleared. I sent doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 10 days to your pharmacy. Take it with water and stay upright for a bit after, and go easy on direct sun. If you get a fever, the cough gets worse, or you're not better when you finish this, I need to see you in person.

reports.conclusion: Bilateral nodular infiltrates. Recommend clinical correlation and further evaluation.

orders.reason: bilateral nodular infiltrates, hemoptysis, weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Sinuses never cleared after two antibiotic courses, going on close to two months now. Cough brings up phlegm and a few times there have been streaks of blood. Down about 10 lb since July without trying. Feels run down, and his joints are aching in a different way than before, more all over. No fever he has measured. No rash.

O: Weight 99.5 kg (104 in July). Afebrile, sats normal on room air. Nasal mucosa crusted. Scattered expiratory wheeze both sides. Heart regular. No rash, no lymphadenopathy.
CXR in office: multiple nodular opacities in both lungs.

A/P: Refractory sinus disease, hemoptysis, weight loss, joint aches and bilateral lung nodules. Worried about a systemic process (vasculitis, infection, malignancy all on the list). Called pulmonology directly, they will see him 3/8. Told him to go to the ED for anything more than streaks of blood or for shortness of breath. Holding off on more antibiotics.

conditions.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis with renal involvement

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group
Visit date: 3/8/2023
Referred for: bilateral lung nodules

50 year old man with acromegaly from a pituitary macroadenoma, on octreotide since November, who has had sinus symptoms since early January that did not respond to two courses of antibiotics. Over the same stretch, a productive cough with intermittent small-volume hemoptysis, about 10 lb of weight loss, general malaise, and joint pains that are new and separate from his acromegalic arthropathy.

Meds per patient: lisinopril, HCTZ, albuterol as needed, octreotide LAR. NKDA. Never smoker. Heavy daily alcohol.

Exam: afebrile. BP 145/90. Diffuse wheezes throughout both lung fields. Skin without rash.

Data: chest radiograph from his PCP 2/23 reviewed, bilateral nodular infiltrates. Urinalysis today: blood 2+, red blood cell casts on microscopy. Creatinine 2.8, up from 1.0 last year. Normocytic anemia, hemoglobin 11.2. ESR 72.

Impression: upper airway disease, pulmonary nodules with hemoptysis and an active urinary sediment with rising creatinine. This picture is granulomatosis with polyangiitis until proven otherwise, with renal involvement.

Plan: ANCA serologies sent. Urgent rheumatology referral, which I have arranged for next week; they will direct induction therapy and involve nephrology as needed. CT chest at their discretion. He knows to go to the ED for heavier bleeding or breathlessness.

documents.title: Call with patient
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonology called me yesterday afternoon with their impression. Called Keith on his lunch. Explained GPA in plain terms, that the kidneys are involved and that treatment is usually steroids plus an infusion drug, and that it generally works. Rheumatology appointment 3/14 confirmed. Asked him to hold off on ibuprofen and to drink less, ideally none, given the kidneys. He was quiet but asked good questions. Will see him after rheumatology starts treatment.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth daily, then taper per rheumatology
IV infusion at the rheumatology infusion center per rheumatology (induction 375 mg/m2 weekly x4, then maintenance)

medications.drug: sulfamethoxazole 800 MG / trimethoprim 160 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times weekly (Mon, Wed, Fri)

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice
Seen 3/14/2023

Assessment: ANCA-associated vasculitis, clinically granulomatosis with polyangiitis, with sinus, pulmonary (nodules, hemoptysis) and renal (RBC casts, creatinine 2.8) involvement. Organ-threatening disease.

Plan:
- Prednisone 60 mg daily, taper over roughly 5 to 6 months per the schedule given to him.
- Rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly x 4, first infusion this week.
- Hepatitis B surface antigen negative and hepatitis C antibody negative today, cleared for rituximab.
- TMP-SMX DS three times a week for PJP prophylaxis while on prednisone.
- Weekly BMP and CBC for the first month, then with PCP visits.
- Discussed alcohol and steroids, bone and stomach protection, and infection precautions. He was advised to hold off on live vaccines.

Current medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, albuterol as needed, octreotide LAR 20 mg monthly, plus the above. NKDA.

documents.title: Infusion scheduling
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Rheumatology infusion nurse called to confirm our office has no conflicting orders and to ask for his last CBC. Faxed 3/8 pulmonology labs. First rituximab infusion tomorrow.

documents.title: Can't sleep
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it normal to be wide awake at 2am on this prednisone? Also hungry all the time. Wife says I'm short with everybody.

documents.title: RE: Can't sleep
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very normal at 60 mg, unfortunately. Take the whole dose first thing in the morning, not later in the day. It gets better as the dose comes down. If the moods get to be more than irritability, call me. And the alcohol makes all of this harder, sleep included.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up GPA. Four rituximab infusions done. Prednisone now 40 mg on the taper sheet.
Sinuses much better, cough nearly gone, no blood since mid-March. Joints less achy. Sleep still poor. Drinking 'less', he says maybe 4 to 6 a night.

BP 142/88, afebrile. Nasal crusting improved. Lungs clear today. Moon face starting. No edema.

Labs today: creatinine 1.9 (2.8 at diagnosis), hemoglobin 11.9, UA still 1+ blood.

A/P:
- GPA with renal involvement, responding. Rheumatology following; copied them on labs.
- Sinusitis label closed, this was the vasculitis.
- HTN slightly above goal on prednisone, no change yet.
- PCV20 today given immunosuppression and alcohol use.
- Alcohol: acknowledged the cutback, encouraged more. Still not interested in medication.
RTC 2 months.

documents.title: Labs from today
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Keith, your kidney number came down from 2.8 to 1.9, which is real progress, and your blood count is starting to recover. Rheumatology has the results. Keep the TMP-SMX going three days a week.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for TMP-SMX DS refill. Prescribed by rheumatology. Called pharmacy and redirected to the rheumatology office. Albuterol refilled per protocol, last fill 5 months ago.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Prednisone down to 15 mg. No sinus trouble, no cough, no blood. Back to full days on site. Weight has come back and then some (103 kg). Still getting octreotide monthly.
BP 138/84. Lungs clear. No edema.
Creatinine 1.4, Hgb 13.0, urine dip clean today.

A/P: GPA in good response, kidney function recovering. Continue rheumatology plan. BP acceptable. Shingrix #1 today (recombinant, fine with rituximab); #2 in the fall. Alcohol still most days, discussed again briefly. RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.4 and hemoglobin 13.0, both moving the right way, and the urine is clean. Nice work.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice
Seen 9/5/2023

GPA in clinical remission. No sinus, chest or joint complaints. Prednisone taper finished this week. TMP-SMX stopped along with it.
Plan: rituximab 500 mg maintenance in October, then every 6 months. BMP, CBC and urinalysis every 3 months. Return in 3 months.
Medications: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, albuterol, octreotide LAR. NKDA.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second Shingrix L deltoid, flu R deltoid, 2023-24 COVID R deltoid (separate site). No prior reactions except a sore arm after the first Shingrix. Observed 15 min, fine. Off prednisone as of this month per pt.
